root_cause: SIGMA_ARTIFACT_FORMAT_CHANGE: commit 5c3a3d3 (2026-05-22) introduced STEP 9 in run_results_sigma.py which writes a local sigma artifact containing ONLY aggregate stats (sr, wins, misses, etc.) with NO per-race rows[] array. Prior sigma files (May 21 - Jun 05) used a different script/format ('racing_post_supported_sigma') that DID include rows[] arrays with per-race velo_prime_prob. From Jun 06 onwards, run_results_sigma.py produced 'sigma_reconciliation' format artifacts with no rows[] array, so per-race VP is absent from local artifacts. IMPORTANT: VP calculation was never broken. Supabase sigma_audits retains VP for all rows. The local mirror artifact simply lost the per-race data.

root_cause_detail.format_change_commit: 5c3a3d3 (2026-05-22): fix(sigma): write local Sigma result artifact for Council

race_id_format_change.note: Jun 06 used formatted race IDs (rp_CHP_20260606_5.10). Jun 07+ switched to numeric IDs (920088). Both formats have VP in top object of verdict JSON. This ID format change is NOT the VP loss cause.

local_backup_analysis.filtering_effect: today_race_ids filter can drop entire races from predictions dict (not strip VP from surviving rows)

forensic_questions.Q4_381_row_subset_source: rows[] arrays in sigma_results_*.json files with source='racing_post_supported_sigma' (May 21 - Jun 05). These 461 rows had VP. The 381 refers to a subset used in a specific VP-band analysis.
forensic_questions.Q6_causative_commit: 5c3a3d3 (2026-05-22) added STEP 9 artifact writer without rows[]. This ran for Jun 06 onwards as run_results_sigma.py replaced the old racing_post_supported_sigma workflow.
forensic_questions.Q7_why_field_missing: ARTIFACT_FORMAT_CHANGE: sigma writer stopped writing per-race rows[] array. VP calculation itself is intact in Supabase.

sigma_subset_source: rows[] arrays from sigma_results files with source=racing_post_supported_sigma used in VP-band analysis

sigma_results_YYYY_MM_DD.json.rows: array of per-race objects with velo_prime_prob, vp_source, vp_provenance, vp_recovered, vp_missing_reason
sigma_results_YYYY_MM_DD.json.vp_coverage: object with total_rows, rows_with_vp, rows_missing_vp, vp_source

vp_by_winner_sp_band.note: From pre-Jun-06 rows[] data: VP >= 0.30 n=125 SR=38%, VP >= 0.35 n=88 SR=44%, VP >= 0.40 n=64 SR=48%, VP >= 0.45 n=46 SR=54%. Monotonic relationship confirmed. VP does correlate with shorter-priced picks but is NOT simply a price filter — the ensemble generates VP from SQPE + improvement_score + market_deception_score, not from SP directly.
vp_by_winner_sp_band.correlation_with_short_price: partial — VP reflects model confidence which tends to be higher for form horses that also tend to be shorter prices, but high-VP outsider winners exist

vp_by_course.note: Insufficient per-race VP rows in local artifacts for Jun 07+ to segment by course. Supabase sigma_audits would be needed for full analysis. Small-n course warning: any course with fewer than 15 sigma rows should be flagged INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLE before drawing SR conclusions.

vp_by_field_size.note: Not computable from current local artifact data. Verdict JSON files have field size (scored field) but not linked to sigma outcome rows without a join.

vp_proxying_short_price.evidence: VP is computed from SQPE v17 (form/class model), improvement_score, and market_deception_score. All three can fire independently of price. High-MDS runners can have high VP at generous prices. The SR-VP monotonic relationship reflects model calibration quality, not just price compression.

frame_rate_predicts_next_day_sr.note: Frame rate (VP correlation) appears to predict day-level calibration quality but daily sample sizes (28-57 races) are too small for next-day SR prediction. No rule built.
